sections.title: What you get at each price tier
sections.description: Understanding what's included at each price point helps you scope the right level of ML investment for your use case.

blocks.heading: Classification & Prediction — Tabular Data ($25,000–$90,000)
paragraphs: The most common ML category — predicting a binary or multi-class outcome from structured tabular data.
bullets: Standard ($25K–$40K): Single prediction target, existing labeled data, standard ML stack (XGBoost/LightGBM), FastAPI endpoint, basic dashboard, 2–3 months monitoring
Complex ($40K–$65K): Multi-feature from 3–6 data sources, custom data pipeline, explainability (SHAP), A/B testing framework, CRM/ERP integration
Enterprise ($65K–$90K): FCRA adverse action codes, ECOA disparate impact testing, SR 11-7 documentation, audit trail, MLOps with drift detection

blocks.heading: Time-Series Forecasting ($30,000–$100,000)
paragraphs: Predicting future values from historical sequences — demand forecasting, price prediction, energy load forecasting.
bullets: Standard ($30K–$50K): Single target metric, ARIMA/Prophet/XGBoost with time features, seasonality/holiday effects, forecast accuracy dashboard
Complex ($50K–$75K): Hundreds/thousands of individual series, hierarchical coherence, external regressors (weather, promotions), automated model selection
Enterprise ($75K–$100K): Millions of series, real-time forecast updates, ERP integration, scenario analysis, probabilistic forecasting

blocks.heading: Natural Language Processing ($35,000–$120,000)
paragraphs: ML models that understand, classify, or extract from text.
bullets: Standard ($35K–$55K): Document/sentence classification or NER, fine-tuned transformer (BERT/RoBERTa), batch processing API, performance evaluation
Complex ($55K–$85K): Classification + extraction + summarization, domain-specific fine-tuning, multiple entity types, human review workflow
Enterprise ($85K–$120K): Clinical NLP with HIPAA, legal NLP with privilege requirements, financial NLP with SEC/FINRA compliance, multi-language support, full explainability

blocks.heading: Anomaly Detection & Fraud ML ($40,000–$130,000)
paragraphs: Detecting outliers, anomalies, and fraudulent behavior.
bullets: Standard ($40K–$60K): Univariate/multivariate anomaly detection, Isolation Forest/LOF/Autoencoder, threshold tuning, alert routing
Complex ($60K–$90K): Labeled fraud examples for supervised classification, real-time scoring API, transaction sequence features, feedback loop from fraud team
Enterprise ($90K–$130K): Sub-100ms scoring at payment processor throughput, graph-based fraud ring detection, distributed feature computation, FCRA compliance

blocks.heading: Computer Vision ($50,000–$200,000)
paragraphs: See the full Computer Vision Development Cost guide for application-specific pricing.

sections.title: Three variables that determine your ML model cost
sections.description: Understanding these drivers helps you budget realistically and scope the right project for your needs.

items.title: 1. Data Preparation (30–40% of project cost)
items.description: Most enterprise ML projects spend more time on data preparation than on modeling. Variables include label acquisition ($1K–$30K), data integration from multiple sources, and quality remediation for missing values, outliers, and systematic issues.
items.label: Data Readiness

items.title: 2. Compliance & Documentation
items.description: ML compliance requirements add 25–50% to basic model cost: SR 11-7 validation ($15K–$35K), FCRA adverse action codes ($8K–$18K), FDA SaMD ($20K–$50K), HIPAA BAA ($8K–$18K), ECOA disparate impact ($6K–$14K).
items.label: Regulatory

items.title: 3. Production Infrastructure
items.description: Building the production ML system (not just the model) adds 30–40% to model-only cost: REST API & containerization ($5K–$12K), automated retraining pipeline ($8K–$18K), monitoring & alerting ($5K–$12K), load testing ($3K–$8K).
items.label: Deployment

sections.title: ML model cost vs. ROI — the calculation that matters
sections.description: The most important cost question isn't 'how much does ML cost?' — it's 'what is this ML worth?'

blocks.heading: Churn Prediction
paragraphs: Monthly churn: 2,000 customers × $500 avg CLV = $1,000,000/month lost. ML reduces churn by 10% = $100,000/month saved = $1.2M/year. ML development cost: $50,000. ROI: 24x in first year.

blocks.heading: Demand Forecasting
paragraphs: Current forecast error: 25% MAPE. Excess inventory from forecast error: $500,000 in safety stock. ML reduces MAPE to 12% = $200,000+ inventory reduction. ML development cost: $65,000. ROI: 3x in first year on inventory alone.

blocks.heading: Fraud Detection
paragraphs: Current fraud losses: $2M/year on $100M transactions (2% fraud rate). ML reduces fraud rate to 0.8% = $1.2M/year recovered. ML development cost: $90,000 (real-time, high-volume). ROI: 13x in first year.

items.objection: What does machine learning model development cost?
items.answer: $25,000–$200,000 depending on problem type, data availability, and compliance requirements. Most enterprise ML projects: $40,000–$100,000.

items.objection: How long does ML model development take?
items.answer: 8–32 weeks. Simple classification on existing data: 8–12 weeks. Enterprise fraud ML with sub-100ms real-time scoring: 18–28 weeks.

items.objection: What is the most common reason ML projects run over budget?
items.answer: Data problems discovered after the project starts—missing labels, inaccessible systems, poor data quality, or schema changes. ClickMasters addresses this in a paid Discovery phase before full project commitment.

items.objection: Does ClickMasters build ML models that work in production, or just research models?
items.answer: Production ML systems—including data pipeline, API serving, monitoring, and MLOps infrastructure. ClickMasters doesn't deliver Jupyter notebooks; we deliver production ML systems that operate reliably in your infrastructure.

items.objection: What's the difference between ML model development cost and fine-tuning cost?
items.answer: ML model development involves custom feature engineering and model architecture choices. Fine-tuning adapts an existing foundation model to your domain. ML development is for structured data; fine-tuning is for language generation and comprehension tasks.

sections.title: Questions to ask any ML development vendor before hiring

blocks.heading: Six questions that reveal whether a vendor has shipped real ML systems
paragraphs: 1. Do you deliver production ML systems (deployed and monitored) or research models (Jupyter notebooks)?
2. Is the price fixed or time-and-materials?
3. Do we own all IP and model weights at project close?
4. What happens if the model doesn't meet performance targets?
5. Do you have experience with our compliance requirements (FCRA, HIPAA, SR 11-7)?
6. Can you provide references from similar ML projects?

blocks.heading: ClickMasters answers all of these directly
paragraphs: Production systems, fixed-price, full IP, performance targets in the contract, compliance expertise, and references on request.
